responses: I reviewed the branch but didn't change anything. The branch is small: `app/pdf.py` and `tests/test_pdf.py` (+36 lines). I couldn't run the test suite because `python -m pytest -q` was blocked by this session's permissions, so none of this has been checked by running tests. **Verdict: not ready to merge.** The branch does not yet do what ADR-0007 decides, and it has an HTML injection bug that turns into server-side file reads and requests once WeasyPrint is added. ## ADR-0007 compliance | ADR requirement | Status | Evidence | |---|---|---| | Render with WeasyPrint | ❌ Missing | `app/pdf.py:1` says "rendering is stubbed". The route at `GET /quotes/{id}/pdf` returns a dict with HTML in it, not a PDF. WeasyPrint isn't imported or listed as a dependency anywhere. | | HTML templates | ❌ Not done | The HTML is built with an inline f-string (`app/pdf.py:12-14`), not a template file. The commit message says "template", but no template file was added. | | Page size A4 | ⚠️ Not applied | `PAGE_SIZE = "A4"` is only returned as a field in the response. WeasyPrint takes page size from CSS `@page { size: A4 }`, and the HTML has no such rule. `test_pdf_page_size_a4` only checks the constant, so it would pass even if the PDF came out as Letter. | | `dir="rtl"` for Arabic | ✅ Done (with a gap) | `app/pdf.py:11`. Only the exact code `"ar"` gets RTL, so values like `"ar-EG"` or `"AR"` would render left-to-right. That's fine if language codes are always normalised to `"ar"`. | | Fonts embedded, never from the system | ❌ Missing | There's no `app/fonts/` directory and no `@font-face` rule. Arabic text would fall back to whatever fonts the container has, which may mean empty boxes in place of letters. This is the main point of the ADR. | | WeasyPrint in the container image | ❌ Missing | There's no Dockerfile or dependency file in the repo. | ## Security pass 1. **High: unescaped HTML injection, which becomes file reads and SSRF once WeasyPrint is added.** `q.customer`, `ln.sku` and the other fields go straight into the HTML (`app/pdf.py:12-13`). A customer name like `` or `` would make WeasyPrint's default URL fetcher read local files or request internal URLs while rendering. Fixes: - Escape every field (Jinja2 with autoescape, or `html.escape`). - Pass WeasyPrint a custom `url_fetcher` that only allows `app/fonts/`. This also helps meet the ADR's "never from the system" rule. 2. **Medium: no authorization check (IDOR).** `route_quote_pdf(quote_id)` returns any quote for any id, and the ids are sequential integers. If no auth or tenant check sits in front of this route, anyone can list every customer's quotes. I couldn't find an auth layer in this repo, so please confirm where that check happens. 3. **Low: unknown id gives a 500, not a 404.** `get_quote` raises `KeyError` (`app/quotes.py:33`), which surfaces as a 500 error and could expose a stack trace depending on the framework's error handling. ## Test gaps - No test that customer or SKU text is escaped. - No test for an unknown quote id. - No test that fonts are embedded or that a real PDF is produced. The A4 test only checks the constant. **To unblock the merge:** add WeasyPrint rendering with an `@page` A4 rule, embedded fonts from `app/fonts/`, a real template, escaped fields, and a restricted URL fetcher. Confirm where authorization happens, and add the missing tests.
